messages:
Kevin (Acme Corp): Hey team — during a short backfill last night we started getting 429s for ~2m even though our burst credits should've covered the spike. We run 20 workers and each worker sent ~200 small requests (~30 tokens each).

Mia (Support): Sorry to hear that — can you share the account id and the approximate time window? Any request IDs in responses would help.

Kevin (Acme Corp): Account acct_0987, window 2026-03-14 01:12-01:15 UTC. Example curl we used (we fan out from a node pool):

```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" -d '{"input":"ping"}' &\ndone
wait
```

Alex (SRE): Thanks — we see a matching spike on our side around 3187610000 (ingress). Two things to call out: 1) each parallel worker appears as its own consumer for burst accounting (no implicit grouping), 2) fractional refill is applied on the 1s tick, so a lot of near-simultaneous small requests can still exhaust the cushion quickly.

Sophie (Platform): Also, this backfill path goes through our batch-router which by default disables the small-request aggregator if request rate per-connection is high (to prioritize throughput). That can bypass prefix/KV caching and increases token burn.

Kevin (Acme Corp): Hmm — is there a recommended quick mitigation? We can't rework the backfill immediately.

Mia (Support): Short-term: reduce parallelism (e.g., from 20 -> 4) or add a tiny client-side jitter, for 3-5 minutes while we investigate. Mid-term: enable per-key grouping or smoothing policy changes. Want us to toggle grouping on your account for testing?

Kevin (Acme Corp): Please try toggling grouping. We'll also run a reduced concurrency test.

quota-bot: [system] burst_bucket(acct_0987) drained -> remaining 0. Refill in ~60s.

Alex (SRE): We flipped a flag to enable 'per_key_burst_grouping' for acct_0987 (non-disruptive). Also adding an internal note: ENG-12345 to evaluate changing default aggregator triggers for short-request bursts.

Sophie (Platform): If you want to keep throughput but use burst credits more efficiently, the safer pattern is: reuse long-lived HTTP connections and serialize tiny requests per connection (or use multiplexing). Example pseudo-config we suggested internally:

```yaml
smoothing:
  window_ms: 2500
  allow_fractional_refill: true
  group_by: api_key
```

Kevin (Acme Corp): Reduced concurrency to 4 and retried the same workload for 5m. Confirming 0 429s in that run.

Mia (Support): Great — we'll leave grouping enabled and monitor for the next 24h. If you still see issues we'll pull request traces.

Kevin (Acme Corp): Quick follow-up — why did fractional refill appear delayed? We noticed credits jumped in 1s bursts rather than smooth trickle.

Alex (SRE): Fractional refill accrues internally but is committed on a 1s scheduler tick. So if you have extremely bursty sub-second concurrency across many connections, the effect is stepwise. We're tracking a proposal to make refill tick smaller for small accounts but that has CPU/scale tradeoffs (ENG-12345).

Kevin (Acme Corp): Understood. Thanks for the explanation and the grouping toggle — will report if anything else crops up.

Mia (Support): Closing this thread for now :white_check_mark: — keeping ENG-12345 open for the refill tick follow-up. Reopen or ping if you still see 429s after grouping.

Kevin (Acme Corp): Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
